neighbours.label: the magical other world of a classic portal fantasy, where a child is carried away (Oz, Wonderland, Narnia, Looking-Glass)
fire: In the film, a tornado lifts the farmhouse and sets it down in the Land of Oz.
The children climb through the back of the wardrobe and find themselves in snowy Narnia.
Our school play this year is Alice's Adventures in Wonderland.
In Through the Looking-Glass, Alice steps into a world where everything runs backwards.
Miyazaki's Spirited Away follows a girl trapped in a world of spirits.
The Wizard of Oz is still shown on television every year at Thanksgiving.
Wendy and her brothers follow the second star to the right, all the way to Neverland.
Coraline finds a small door in her new house that opens onto an Other World.
quiet: In the film, a pig named Wilbur is saved by a spider who writes words in her web.
The children spend the summer on their grandfather's farm and learn to ride horses.
Our school play this year is Little Women, with four sisters on stage.
In Black Beauty, a horse tells the story of his life with many different owners.
Miyazaki's My Neighbor Totoro follows two sisters who move to the countryside.
Winnie-the-Pooh is still read aloud in classrooms every year in the autumn.
Heidi and her grandfather spend the winter in a hut high in the Swiss mountains.
Matilda finds that she loves reading and visits the library every afternoon.

notes: Card: ' Oz' x4, Dorothy x3, Looking Glass, Alice's Adventures, Spirited Away: all stories where a child is transported to another world. Probe: Wonderland 0.64, Oz 0.52, Narnia 0.43, Neverland 0.20, Dorothy in Kansas 0.13. Near misses are other classic children's stories with no portal world.
